source.name: Tab after typing a date must move to the next field, not jump back into the date field
source.scope: Open upstream bug (https://github.com/Pikaday/Pikaday/issues/827) at 9a90eea5cdbc48784d3a909ddb36e052c16bf25d, unfixed when pinned. Routing Super, then Ultra.

journey.title: Type a check-in date, then Tab to the guests field
journey.goal: After typing a date and pressing Tab, focus stays on the next field so the user can keep filling the form

functionalJourney.title: Pick a check-in day with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day fills the check-in date and the guests field still takes input

guards.title: Paging months with the pointer keeps keyboard focus in the date field
guards.goal: After clicking Next month, focus is back in the date field so arrow keys and typing keep working

plan.root_cause: The Pikaday draw method refocuses the input trigger after showing the calendar, preventing keyboard navigation away from the date field when the user presses Tab.
plan.repair_strategy: Remove the automatic refocus of the trigger bound to the input within the draw method, allowing focus to move to the next focusable element (e.g., the guests field) on Tab.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: After entering a date and pressing Tab, focus will move to the guests field, enabling keyboard-only users to continue filling the form without being trapped in the date picker.
functional_risks: Removing the auto-refocus may cause the input to lose focus when the calendar is shown programmatically, potentially affecting users who expect the field to remain focused after opening the picker via script.
Mouse users who click the field to open the picker will still retain focus because the field already has focus; the refocus was only redundant.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab after entering a date moves focus to the guests field.
Confirm that date selection via mouse or keyboard still updates the input value correctly.
Ensure that pressing Esc or Enter closes the picker and returns focus to the input field.
Check that the picker still opens when the input receives focus.
